summary:
## Background
Abacavir is an antiretroviral used for HIV treatment that can cause a clinically significant hypersensitivity reaction (HSR). This study analyzed 248 abacavir-exposed individuals (18 definite HSR cases; 230 tolerant controls) from the Western Australian HIV Cohort to fine-map genetic risk within the MHC region.

## Key Findings
- HLA-B*57:01 showed a very strong association with abacavir HSR:
  - Present in 94.4% of HSR cases vs 1.7% of controls; OR = 960; Pc < 0.00001.
  - In a prospective subset, HSR incidence among HLA-B*57:01–negative individuals was 0% (95% CI 0–0.075%).
  - Predictive performance (retrospective cohort): PPV 78.9%, NPV 99.4%.
- A nonsynonymous variant in Hsp70-Hom (HSPA1L M493T; rs2227956) co-inherited on the 57.1 ancestral haplotype further refined risk:
  - Alone: present in 94.4% of cases vs 22.2% of controls; OR = 59.7; Pc < 0.00001.
  - In combination with HLA-B*57:01: 94.4% of cases vs 0.4% of controls; OR = 3,893; Pc < 0.00001.
  - Predictive performance for the combination: PPV 93.8%, NPV 99.5%; significantly improved discrimination vs HLA-B*57:01 alone (P = 0.003).
- Other markers on the 57.1 ancestral haplotype were associated but less discriminative:
  - C4A6: OR = 111; HLA-DRB1*07:01/HLA-DQ3: OR = 70; the full haplotype (HLA-B*57:01, C4A6, DRB1*07:01/DQ3) had OR = 1,485.
- Mechanistic support: Ex vivo abacavir stimulation increased monocyte TNF in HSR cases; the response was abrogated by CD8+ T-cell depletion, consistent with an HLA class I–restricted, HLA-B*57:01–mediated immune response.

## Clinical Implications
- Pre-treatment HLA-B*57:01 genotyping robustly identifies patients at high risk for abacavir HSR and can effectively prevent reactions; in this cohort, ~14 patients would need screening to prevent one HSR.
- Adding Hsp70-Hom M493T to HLA-B*57:01 testing may further increase specificity and reduce unnecessary exclusion from abacavir (projected HSR prevalence reduced from 8% to 0.4% with combined testing in this cohort).
- Patients who carry HLA-B*57:01—especially those also carrying Hsp70-Hom M493T—should avoid abacavir. These findings are particularly applicable in populations of European descent where HLA-B*57:01 is more prevalent.
